text:
mike: heads up — noticed a small but reproducible spike in client resume failures on streaming endpoints after a transient proxy restart. ~0.5% of sessions never get the resume ACK and clients stay in reconnect loop.

nora: any logs or example client traces?

mike: here's one from a user session (trimmed):
```
SSE: \u003cstream chunk id=34\u003e {events: [... partial chunk ...]}
client: resume(token=abc123, seq=345)
server: 200 OK (no payload)  <-- expected resume_ack but nothing
client: keepalive then reconnect
```

sasha: does the server silently coalesce/multiplex ACKs? we added a resume coalescing optimization last month to reduce small writes. if the ACK is combined with a later chunk the client may time out waiting for the ACK and then send a resume with a token that's already advanced. routing/proxy could also drop the later ACK when quota/billing header mismatch happens.

mike: interesting — we do see a pattern where the proxy returns 429-level quota header then the backend emits the ACK in same write. client times out waiting for ACK and submits resume; backend sees stale token and drops it.

priya: that rings a bell — console rollout:stream.resume_coalesce was flipped on in the EU canary last week to reduce tail CPU. rollout notes said "coalesce small ACKs into one write". did we add telemetry for resume-surface? iirc we never emitted a metric for "resume_ack_sent" per shard.

ryan: confirmed: rollout flag enabled at 2026-03-18T02:13:00Z for eu-canary. telemetry gap: we only log a counter when full resume completes, not on the low-level ACK. dashboard has no metric for ACK latency so hard to see.

mike: repro steps locally: toggle resume_coalesce=true, run proxy simulator with a 50ms jitter, and force a quota rejection header injection. clients that time out (~150ms) end up stuck.

sasha: short-term suggestion: revert the coalesce flag for canary and prod, add a 100ms ACK flush boundary (i.e., flush ACKs immediately when token present), and add a metric resume_ack_sent with labels {region, shard}.

priya: agree — we should revert the flag on canary immediately. then plan a fix to make coalescing safe: if an ACK for resume is pending, always flush that write (or attach an ACK-in-band minimal envelope). also add console UX: show resume ack latency in the streaming route dashboard.

ryan: i can do a quick rollback via the rollout API: POST /internal/rollouts/flags with {flag: "stream.resume_coalesce", value: false, scope: "eu-canary"}. want me to run?

mike: please run it. mark the change with tag rollback/stream-resume-coalesce.

deploy-bot: deploy started — rollout job 29384 by ryan — target: eu-canary, flag: stream.resume_coalesce=false

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded — rollout job 29384 completed (3/3 hosts)

mike: after rollback we saw immediate drop in resume-failure reports for that region in SRE channel. can we keep the flag off until a proper fix lands?

priya: yes. plan: 1) add resume_ack_sent metric + dashboard panel 2) change coalescing logic to flush ACKs or attach explicit ack envelope 3) add unit+integration tests simulating proxy quota headers 4) staged canary with telemetry gating. aiming for PR today and canary next week.

sasha: note for the code change — also make resume handling idempotent: accept resume tokens that are within small window (seq drift <= 1) and reply with a clear protocol code so clients don't assume permanent failure. clients should handle duplicate ACKs idempotently too.

mike: filing follow-up bug: STREAM-1257 — "resume ACK coalescing leads to lost resumes under quota-injection". tagging eng-runtime, eng-platform, and devex for client-side guidance.

ryan: thanks — i'll update the rollout doc and add a quick console alert for resume_error_rate when it spikes >0.2% for 5m.

priya: small telemetry TODOs: 1) emit resume_ack_sent, resume_ack_latency_ms, resume_retries 2) add logs with minimal context (shard, region, token-hash prefix) but avoid PII 3) console panel + alert.

mike: sounds good. leaving this thread open for follow-ups. will post STREAM-1257 link once created. :thumbsup:
